critical_operation.code:
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
RUN pnpm build
RUN pnpm ui:build

CMD ["bash"]
critical_operation.desc: Dependency installation, application builds, and the final bash command all remain under the inherited root identity because no USER instruction intervenes. A compromise therefore starts with uid 0 and amplifies container-breakout impact.

entry_point.desc: FROM starts the image configuration from node:22-bookworm, whose inherited default user is root. With no later USER instruction, this identity remains effective for build steps and the container command.

trace.desc: The base image establishes root as the inherited effective user for this configuration stage.

critical_operation.desc: The entire build context is copied and pnpm install runs as root. Dependency lifecycle scripts therefore receive unnecessary root privilege, and any image derived from this stage also inherits root absent a USER directive.

entry_point.desc: The node:22-bookworm stage begins with root as its default effective user, and this Dockerfile never overrides it.

trace.desc: Base-image user inheritance establishes the privileged configuration state.
The application context and dependency installation execute under the unchanged root identity.

critical_operation.desc: The launcher is installed and selected as ENTRYPOINT without a preceding USER transition. Every invocation of the test entrypoint consequently begins as root.

entry_point.desc: The node:22-bookworm-slim base image supplies root as the default user for this test image.

trace.desc: The image stage inherits root from its base.

  && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \

    curl \
    git \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
trace.desc: Package installation runs in the inherited privileged build context.
The executable is installed and becomes the runtime entrypoint while root remains effective.

critical_operation.code:
RUN useradd -m -s /bin/bash app \
  && echo "app ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL" > /etc/sudoers.d/app
critical_operation.desc: The app user is granted passwordless sudo for ALL commands. Although USER app is selected later, this sudoers rule lets any compromised process recover unrestricted root immediately, defeating the intended privilege boundary.

entry_point.desc: The Ubuntu image starts configuration as root; later instructions create an app account intended to lower runtime privilege.

trace.code:
RUN set -eux; \
  for attempt in 1 2 3; do \
    if apt-get update -o Acquire::Retries=3; then break; fi; \
    echo "apt-get update failed (attempt ${attempt})" >&2; \
    if [ "${attempt}" -eq 3 ]; then exit 1; fi; \
    sleep 3; \
  done; \
  apt-get -o Acquire::Retries=3 install -y --no-install-recommends \
    bash \
    ca-certificates \
    curl \
    sudo \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
trace.desc: The privileged build stage installs sudo, making later privilege recovery available in the image.

trace.desc: The configuration creates app and grants it unrestricted passwordless sudo.
USER app changes the nominal runtime uid but does not remove the NOPASSWD sudo capability.
